author: Chris Schommer
title: Sam Antonacci goes deep in win over Blue Jays
desc: Sam Antonacci went 2-for-5 in a win over the Blue Jays with a home run, two runs scored, and two RBI.
impact: Antonacci continues a productive stretch at the plate, driving in runs in six of his last 10 contests. The outfielder remains one of the more dynamic options in a streaky White Sox lineup for manager Will Venable, carrying an .810 OPS with seven homers, 29 RBI, 50 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases through 76 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Braden Montgomery drives in four, swipes base in win over Blue Jays
desc: Braden Montgomery went 1-for-5 in a win over the Blue Jays with a triple, two runs scored, four RBI, and one stolen base.
impact: Montgomery has heated up at the plate of late, picking up hits in eight of his last 10 contests. The outfielder continues to battle inconsistent stretches since being called up, batting .229 with three home runs, 16 RBI, 17 runs scored, and one stolen base across 30 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Anthony Kay limits damage in win over Blue Jays
desc: Anthony Kay allowed two earned runs one two hits and three walks while striking out five over four innings in Friday's win over the Blue Jays.
impact: Kay continues a solid stretch on the mound of late, allowing two earned runs or less in each of his last three trips to the mound. The left-hander remains one of the more inconsistent arms in the White Sox rotation for manager Will Venable, posting a 4.29 ERA and 1.37 WHIP with a 6-4 record and 2.0 K/BB ratio across 20 appearances.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Jake McCarthy swipes base in loss to Reds
desc: Jake McCarthy went 1-for-3 in a loss to the Reds with one walk and one stolen base.
impact: McCarthy continues a productive stretch at the plate of late, recording hits in 10 of his last 12 contests. The outfielder has rewarded manager Warren Schaeffer with one of the more impactful options in an inconsistent Rockies lineup, carrying an .863 OPS with 10 home runs, 53 RBI, 39 runs scored, and 16 stolen bases across 84 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Willi Castro homers in loss to Reds
desc: Willi Castro went 2-for-4 in a loss to the Reds with a solo home run.
impact: Castro has offered mixed results at the plate of late, collecting hits on six of his last 11 contests. The veteran has provided manager Warren Schaeffer with one of the more stable bats in a streaky Rockies lineup, slashing .264 with eight homers, 38 RBI, 41 runs, and six steals through 83 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Gabriel Hughes solid on mound in loss to Reds
desc: Gabriel Hughes allowed two earned runs on five hits and two walks while striking out six over 5 1/3 innings in Friday's loss to the Reds.
impact: Hughes continues a steady stretch on the mound, allowing two earned runs or less in two of three trips to the mound. The right-hander has offered manager Warren Schaeffer a mostly stable starting option as part of a dismal Rockies rotation to this point, posting a 3.14 ERA and 1.12 WHIP with an 0-1 record and 8.8 K/9 ratio through three appearances.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Shea Langeliers goes yard in blowout loss
desc: Shea Langeliers went 1-for-4 in a loss to the Nationals with a solo home run.
impact: Langeliers has offered mixed results at the plate of late, picking up hits in four of his last nine contests. The catcher provides manager Mark Kotsay with one of the more explosive bats in a streaky Athletics lineup, carrying an .812 OPS with 22 home runs, 47 RBI, 53 runs scored, and two stolen bases through 87 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Tyler Soderstrom homers in loss to Nationals
desc: Tyler Soderstrom went 1-for-3 in a loss to the Nationals with a two-run home run.
impact: Soderstrom has heated up of late, getting on base in four of his last five contests. The outfielder continues to flash explosive potential as part of a streaky Athletics lineup to this point, posting an .817 OPS with 15 home runs, 44 RBI, 44 runs scored, and one stolen base across 85 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Gage Jump shelled early in blowout loss to Nationals
desc: Gage Jump allowed three earned runs on four hits and two walks while striking out eight over 3 2/3 innings in Friday's loss to the Nationals.
impact: Jump has struggled to miss opposing bats of late, allowing three earned runs or more in three of his last four trips to the mound. The left-hander remains one of many inconsistent options in the Athletics rotation for manager Mark Kotsay, posting a 3-5 record and 9.6 K/9 ratio with a 3.78 ERA and 1.32 WHIP through 10 starts.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Joey Ortiz goes deep, swipes base in win over Marlins
desc: Joey Ortiz went 2-for-4 in a win over the Marlins with a solo home run and one stolen base.
impact: Ortiz has heated up at the plate of late, picking up hits in eight of his last 11 contests. The infielder remains one of the more underperforming options in the Brewers lineup for manager Pat Murphy currently, batting .230 with four homers, 23 RBI, 25 runs scored, and six steals through 84 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Logan Henderson efficient on mound in no-decision
desc: Logan Henderson allowed one earned run on three hits while striking out four over five innings in Friday's 2-1 win over the Marlins.
impact: Henderson has offered mixed results since returning, allowing less than two earned runs in one of his last two contests. The right-hander remains another reliable option as part of a deep Brewers starting staff for manager Pat Murphy, carrying a 2.97 ERA and 0.93 WHIP with a 3-1 record and 10.3 K/9 ratio across seven starts.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Peter Lambert whiffs 10 in no-decision
desc: Peter Lambert allowed one earned run on three hits and two walks while striking out 10 over six innings in Friday's loss to the Orioles.
impact: Lambert continues a strong stretch on the mound of late, allowing two earned runs or less in eight of his last nine trips to the mound. The right-hander offers manager Joe Espada one of the more stable options in an inconsistent Astros rotation, posting a 3.03 ERA and 1.11 WHIP with an 8-5 record and 8.9 K/9 ratio across 16 starts.

author: Nate Miller
title: Drake Baldwin drives in five runs Friday night
desc: Drake Baldwin went 3-for-4 with a three-run homer, a walk, five total RBI, and two runs scored in Friday's 15-1 win over the Rangers.
impact: Fresh off his first All-Star appearance, Baldwin got the Braves offense going Friday night with an RBI single in the second. He followed that up with his 16th homer of the season in the fourth inning, adding a fifth RBI with another single in the next frame. Baldwin set a new season high in RBI, coming up just one short of his career mark. Fantasy managers should be very encouraged by this performance.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Gerrit Cole steady on mound in loss to Dodgers
desc: Gerrit Cole allowed two earned runs on four hits and one walk while striking out eight over six innings in Friday's 2-1 loss to the Dodgers.
impact: Cole has provided mixed results on the mound of late, allowing three earned runs or more in four of his last eight trips to the mound. The right-hander continues to work through inconsistent command at times for manager Aaron Boone since returning from an elbow injury, carrying a 3.93 ERA and 1.16 WHIP with a 3-5 record and 9.0 K/9 ratio through 10 starts this season.

author: Nate Miller
title: Michael Harris II doubles twice, drives in three on Friday
desc: Michael Harris II went 2-for-6 with a pair of doubles, three RBI, and one run scored in Friday's 15-1 drubbing of the Rangers.
impact: Arguably one of the most glaring snubs from the NL All-Star team, Harris went right back to work producing for the Braves on coming out of the break. He now have five multi-RBI games so far in July, and he's up to 56 for the season.
